title: PipeFill: Using GPUs During Bubbles in Pipeline-Parallel LLM Training
problem: Pipeline-parallel LLM training leaves substantial GPU idle time (pipeline bubbles) that represents wasted compute capacity at scale.
motivation: At 8K GPUs, pipeline bubbles can consume 30-40% of total compute time. Recovering this idle capacity without disrupting the primary training job would yield significant throughput gains at minimal additional cost.
method: PipeFill schedules independent fill jobs (batch inference, small model training) into pipeline bubble slots using a Pipeline Bubble Instruction (PBI) abstraction, a Fill Job Executor that maps fill work to idle GPU time, and a Fill Job Scheduler that tracks bubble windows and dispatches work. Implemented on DeepSpeed with GPipe and 1F1B schedules.
key_novelty: First system to systematically characterize and exploit pipeline bubble structure for productive secondary workloads, introducing the PBI abstraction that expresses fill work independently of the primary schedule.
contributions: Formal characterization of pipeline bubble patterns in GPipe and 1F1B schedules
Pipeline Bubble Instruction (PBI) abstraction for expressing fill job work units
Fill Job Executor that executes fill work within bubble windows without disrupting primary training
Fill Job Scheduler that dynamically selects and dispatches fill jobs based on bubble availability
DeepSpeed-based implementation evaluated at up to 8K GPUs

metrics.speedup: 1.63x GPU utilization increase (63% improvement) at 8K GPUs
metrics.accuracy: <2% slowdown on primary LLM training job
metrics.other: Fill job throughput scales with pipeline depth and bubble ratio

limitations: Fill jobs must be independent of the primary training job
Bubble windows may be too short for certain fill workloads
Scheduling overhead increases with number of fill job types
